text:
maria: quick RFC follow-up: we need a concrete profile versioning and override model for FP8/INT8/4-bit profiles. proposal: immutable profile versions, explicit allowed_overrides whitelist, two modes (managed vs self-serve), and canary gating.

devin: sounds right. self-serve should only expose runtime-safe knobs (batch_size, max_latency_ms, canary_fraction). disallow per-layer/scaling overrides in self-serve.

omkar: runtime detail: profile_id must be a content checksum used as the cache key for compiled kernels and KV cache formats. any change that could affect kernel codepath must change the profile_id and trigger a recompile. we should reject self-serve overrides that cause recompilation.

jason: ops: recommend canary schedule: 0.5% for 1 hour -> 5% for 2 hours -> 25% steady. automated revert if primary metric delta > threshold at any step. need to decide metric per endpoint (f1_delta_pct, perplexity_delta_pct, exact_match_delta).

carly: product: customers want control but also safety. managed mode = Redwood validates profile + compiles + runs canary. self-serve = limited surface, must acknowledge risk. include a `degradation_budget_pct` field customers set (default 1.0%).

maria: rough profile schema fields to include (text-only here): name, version, profile_id (sha256), base_profile_ref, allowed_overrides[], quality_gate (metric + threshold), canary_defaults (fraction + duration_mins), canary_probe_prompts[], fallback_profile_ref, override_source enum (managed|self-serve).

omkar: runtime constraint: if allowed_overrides contains anything that touches quant scales/per-layer bitwidth, mark the profile as requiring managed mode and force rebuild.

devin: fallback behavior: on canary failure route traffic to fallback_profile_ref (e.g., int8-safe) and emit telemetry event tagging profile_id and override_source. circuit-breaker should block further canary progression for that customer.

jason: action items: ops will produce alert playbook + auto-revert automation. i'll include canary metric thresholds and the rollback automation for the 5% step.

maria: i'll draft the schema PR with explicit immutability rules and the allowed_overrides whitelist. i'll also add telemetry tagging for profile_id, override_source, and canary_step.

carly: i'll assemble guidance for customers on crafting canary_probe_prompts and recommended degradation budgets per workload type.

maria: OK. next: canary-bot, can we gate pipeline runs until schema PR merges?

canary-bot: Pipeline queued: profile-canary/fp8-safe-2026:v1 — awaiting schema PR merge and CI.
